craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as dense-consciousness-is-Śiva; vyabhicāri wonder that division shines undividing (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: eka eva…sa śivaḥ (one ALONE: HE is Śiva — eva + sa insist); vicitraśaktau…grāhyagrāhakabhedaḥ (in VARIEGATED power — division located inside, not against). Rows: 1 (‘supreme light’ closes L1; ‘grasper’ closes L2 — the split-word last, division landing where it belongs: at the end, inside), 9 (grasped/graspers echo), 12 declined — close is declarative stop, not śānta-fall (the verse declares, then shows). Rupture: ‘And there too’ (identity turns to internal division — the verse's whole move). Rejected: ‘yet’ for ‘And there too’ — killed: tatrāpi is inclusive (there TOO), ‘yet’ would make division an objection; ‘very light’ for ‘supreme light’ — killed: param kept. Read aloud: THUS — DENSE self-CON-scious-ness, ONE a-LONE: HE is ŚI-va … AND-there-TOO … SHINES the SPLIT of GRASPED and GRASP-er.

lines: Thus — dense self-consciousness, one alone: He is Śiva, the universe’s supreme light.
And there too, in variegated power, shines the split of grasped and grasper.
l4.sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ svasaṃvidghana eka eva śivaḥ sa viśvasya paraḥ prakāśaḥ | tatrāpi bhātyeva vicitraśaktau grāhyagṛhītṛpravibhāgabhedaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Dense, one own-consciousness is Śiva himself, the universe's supreme light — yet grasper-grasped division still shines within variegated power. → Positive declaration after denial; division within the undivided.
c1_essence: Dense, one own-consciousness is Śiva himself, the universe's supreme light — yet grasper-grasped division still shines within variegated power.
